transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I've just been feeling... wound up, almost all day long. It's like my body is constantly bracing for something. I notice it even when I’m just sitting at my computer for work, or, you know, trying to relax after dinner. It's just this constant tension.
Along with that physical tension, do you find yourself frequently worrying about a lot of different everyday things?

Yes, I really do. My mind just... it keeps going from one concern to another. I'll be thinking about my sister down in Arecibo, and then suddenly I'm worrying if I missed something important at the office, or... or if my husband is okay driving home. It just cycles through things—church commitments, paying the bills. I just always find myself preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet.
About how long have you been experiencing this constant worry and tension?
It's been going on for about thirteen months now. I think it really started right around the time my sister down in Arecibo began needing a lot more help from the family.
Alongside this worry and tension, have you also been experiencing feelings of sadness or a low mood?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel sad or depressed. I'm just... constantly worried and tense, like I said. But my mood itself isn't low. I still enjoy things when my mind lets me focus on them. It's just the anxiety that's the problem, not sadness.
When these worries start, do you find it difficult to control or stop them?

Yes, it is. It's very hard to stop them once they start. I'll actually tell myself, you know, "Daniela, enough, just focus on this report." But... it doesn't really work. One small thought just turns into five more. And before I know it, I've spent half an hour checking my messages or just replaying everything that could go wrong instead of working.
Have you been having any trouble with your sleep, such as falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yes, I have. I mean, most nights I do fall asleep eventually, but staying asleep is the problem. I tend to wake up around three or four in the morning, and my mind just starts going—thinking about my sister's next appointment or some server issue we're having at work. And the frustrating part is, even when I do manage to get enough hours of sleep, I usually start the morning feeling like I never really rested at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits generalized, persistent, and uncontrollable worry across multiple everyday domains (family, work, finances) lasting for 13 months, exceeding the 6-month requirement for generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). Associated symptoms include marked motor tension (feeling wound up, bracing, constant muscle tension) and sleep disturbance (waking early, difficulty staying asleep, unrefreshing sleep) leading to functional distraction at work. Major depressive disorder is ruled out by the patient's explicit denial of low mood or anhedonia.
